title: Claude made a Paper Mario inspired game without refusing
author: Individual_Canary807
selftext:
https://reddit.com/link/1xn9tg0/video/zo0g9w41ohzh1/player

feels like anthropic and other companies are starting to take a stance on ai game dev, and a lot of people here are running into refusals as soon as they mention a real game as a reference.

i've been building games with ai, and i wanted to share what's been working for me. this papercraft 2.5d rpg in the clip is inspired by paper mario, and it was made entirely with ai. no refusals, even when i use existing games as visual and mechanical references.

it runs on Maneki, an agent i built specifically for game dev. it handles the parts general coding agents struggle with and takes games all the way to being playable and shippable very quickly (this game took <2 hours)

feel free to play it here on [itch](https://maneki-engine.itch.io/kamishibai-demo)

i'm opening a small closed beta for people in this community who are actually making games. if you want in, sign up here: [https://manekiengine.com/](https://manekiengine.com/)

happy to answer questions about the workflow in the comments, art and sound are also generated by this agent!

comments.author: EvoZims
comments.body: Hi, interested in how you built this. Could you give more info on how Maneki works exactly? How did you create the sprites and animations, sounds and environments? I find those to be the most difficult for Claude:

replies.author: Individual_Canary807
replies.body:
Think of it as a Claude Code/Codex but made specifically for game dev. It plans everything, write code, and makes assets then plays the game itself.

Consistent art is the part that we put the most work into, but it boils down to creating a good style bible first and using that for each asset moving forward. 

The agent also composed the music and effects itself using the same style bible.

you should sign up, i'd love for you to try it.

comments.author: cheyumaama
comments.body: That's cause this isn't paper mario or the same game. It just uses the same art style which isn't patented, so there's no problem in using other game elements in your own game.

replies.author: Individual_Canary807
replies.body: i agree, it shouldn't be a problem, but i've told Claude before to make a paper mario inspired game, gave it reference images and it didnt want to.
